newsitem.title: UK: Barclays denies rumours of Taylor departure.
newsitem.headline: Barclays denies rumours of Taylor departure.

text.p: Barclays Plc said on Monday its chief executive Martin Taylor had no intention of leaving the British banking giant, countering market speculation about his future.
"Martin Taylor is not leaving Barclays. We don't know where this has come from but it is simply not true," Alison Lambert, Barclays' spokeswoman told Reuters in a frank denial of the rumours.

Lambert said the firm was bemused that a fall in Barclays' share price, which closed down 53.5 pence at 1135.5 pence, had been attributed to the suggestion Taylor was leaving rather than the real cause, which was the Halifax float.

"We are off because of the Halifax," she said. Analysts said institutional investors had sold bank sector shares to pay for their investment in shares in the former building society, which floated on Monday at the higher end of expectations.
There were widespread suggestions that Taylor, who last month was appointed by Britain's new Labour government to head a taskforce on tax and benefits, was on the point of leaving Barclays.

Taylor, who will spend about two days a month on the project to streamline and modernise the tax and benefits system, told Reuters at the time of his appointment his new role would not affect his position at Barclays.
"There is bound to be a lot of reading involved but I have no intention of it interfering with my role at Barclays," said Taylor, who was appointed as Barclays' chief in 1993.

Barclays also dismissed any suggestion it had planned to sell off its BZW investment banking arm. A recent newspaper report said Germany's Commerzbank had been interested in buying BZW, which Barclays has spent the last 10 years building up.

Reports that Barclays might hive off BZW, which has proved a heavy investment for the bank, or sell it to another bank have resurfaced from time to time but Barclays has always denied it has any such aim.
